# Interway

> Interway is a free route planner for boats on European inland waterways and coastal seas ("Google Maps for
> boats"). It finds routes through rivers, canals, lakes and locks, joins them to a sea route network
> (Baltic, North Sea, Channel, Atlantic coast, Mediterranean, Black Sea), and lists what a route passes: locks
> (with chamber sizes), bridges (with clearance), marinas, ports, fuel, water, pump-outs and towns.
> Routing runs in the browser from OpenStreetMap data. Not for navigation.

## How an AI assistant can use it

The page URL fully describes a route. Write a link, give it to the user, and they open it:

    https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=LON,LAT&to=LON,LAT

Parameters (decimal degrees, longitude first):

- `from`, `to`: start and destination, `lon,lat`
- `via`: waypoints in order, `lon,lat;lon,lat` (use these to force a particular way, e.g. through a canal)
- `draft`, `air` (air draft), `beam`, `len`: vessel dimensions in metres; routes avoid waterways too small
  (defaults: draft 1 m, air draft 3 m, beam 0.5 m, length 9 m: pass the real boat's values)
- `speed`: cruising speed, km/h; `current`: assumed river current, m/s; `lockmin`: minutes per lock
- `avoidLocks=1`: prefer routes with fewer locks
- `avoidSea=1`: keep to inland waterways wherever an inland way exists (open sea already counts 1.5x by default)
- `coastal=1`: for a small boat, keep near the coast (within about 10 km of land), harbour to harbour, instead
  of crossing open sea (e.g. round the Gulf of Lion rather than straight across)

Examples:

- Wrocław to Amsterdam: https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=17.035,51.115&to=4.90,52.38
- Warsaw to Gdańsk on the Vistula, 1.2 m draft: https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=21.03,52.25&to=18.66,54.35&draft=1.2
- London to Crete by sea: https://abecadel.github.io/interway/?from=-0.075,51.507&to=25.14,35.345

## Route brief

After a route is computed the user can press "Copy brief for AI" and paste a Markdown brief into the chat:
distance and time, locks, open-sea distance, towns, legs, daily stages, every stop with its kilometre, vessel
checks against lock chambers and bridge clearances, hazards, and the route link with these parameters. "JSON"
downloads the same brief as structured data.

## Site tools (WebMCP)

In browsers with WebMCP (`document.modelContext`, e.g. the ChatGPT desktop app's built-in browser) the page
registers tools an agent can call directly: `plan_route`, `get_route_brief`, `set_vessel`, `add_waypoint`,
`remove_waypoint`, `find_place` and `list_stops`.

## Coverage and limits

- Inland: Poland, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, France, the United Kingdom (Thames, Broads, the Canal & River Trust and Scottish canals), Austria, Czechia, Slovakia, the Danube to the Black Sea (Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria), northern Italy (the Po, its idrovie and the Litoranea Veneta; lakes Garda, Maggiore, Como), Ireland and Northern Ireland (Shannon, Shannon–Erne Waterway, Erne, Grand and Royal canals, Barrow) Sweden (Göta kanal, Trollhätte kanal, Vänern, Vättern, Mälaren and the canals off them), Finland (the Saimaa lake system and its canals), Lithuania (Nemunas from Kaunas, Neris, Curonian Lagoon), the Vistula and Szczecin lagoons, Spain (Guadalquivir to Seville, Ría de Bilbao, lower Guadiana), Portugal (Douro to Pocinho with its locks, Tejo, Sado, Guadiana), Denmark (Limfjord), Norway (Telemark Canal, Skien → Dalen, and down to the sea at Langesund through Porsgrunn), Estonia (Emajõgi, Lake Peipus), Latvia (Daugava, Lielupe), and the Danube from Kelheim to all three delta arms (Kilia, Sulina, Sfântu Gheorghe). English narrow canals take boats up to 2.08 m (7 ft) beam.
- When no route fits the vessel, the error names each structure that blocks it and its limit (e.g. "Staircase Top Lock
  Gate (km 20) limits beam to 2.08 m, yours is 3 m"); if the points are not connected at all, it says so.
- Navigation mode ("Start navigation" under a route, in the browser with GPS): the map follows the boat heading up and shows the next lock or bridge, speed and course over ground, cross-track error and ETA; it re-plans from the boat's position when it leaves the route, warns before locks and bridges (vibration, optional voice) and records a GPX track. "Save map for offline" stores the map along a route. These have no URL parameters.
- Sea: European seas from the Atlantic coast to the Black Sea, including the whole Mediterranean with harbours and marinas of every coastal country (Greece and the Corinth Canal, Turkey, Malta, Cyprus, the Adriatic, North Africa), as a coarse coastal network.
- Sea depth: open-sea legs carry the charted depth from EMODnet bathymetry (about 0.5 km grid, minus a 0.5 m
  margin). Routes go round stretches too shallow for the given `draft` where a deeper way exists; where none
  does (the coarse network crosses banks that real boats pass in dredged channels, e.g. estuaries) the route
  still goes through, and the brief gives the shallowest stretch and the km charted shallower than the draft.
  The first ~1.5 km off the shore, harbour approaches and inland waterways have no depth data.
- Lock opening hours, closures and current water levels are not included.

Data © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL), towns © GeoNames (CC BY 4.0), bathymetry © EMODnet (CC BY 4.0). Source: https://github.com/abecadel/interway
